chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: The Peckin' dance at the Follies Theater
summary: Spikes first saw Peckin' about 1926 when Esvan Mosby's dance trio performed at the Follies, imitating chickens.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Didn't Esvan Mosby say he...he started what-- "Peckin'"? Didn't he say he...

Well, yeah, I think they did. The first time I seen it, "Peckin'"--you know, when I had the dance...when I had the band at the theater, he had a little trio--dance trio, and they come down there and did this "Peckin'" thing.
That was when you were at The Follies Theatre?
And Esvan Mosby is Curtis Mosby's younger brother, who is a dancer.
Yeah. Yeah. That's the first time I saw the "Peckin'". Yeah.
Esvan told me that it was his invention, that he started it, and I know it was a big hit...what? In the '30s, right? Wasn't that when it was?
No. It was in the...uh, the...'25...'26. '26, I think.
I guess...I became aware of it when I was a child in the '30s.
Well, that's the first time I saw "Peckin'". He had a little trio--three boys--and they [illustrates "Peckin'" moving his head], you know, like chickens. That's the way they'd dance it, you know.
